olivia: Quick benefits question — my partner's child is 21 on an F-1 visa and is returning for the summer/fall term. Can I add them to my medical plan now? Open enrollment is closed so not sure if this is a QLE. What docs would you need?

people-ops: Hi @olivia — short answer: probably yes if they meet dependent criteria (under 26 / your legal child or stepchild). Whether you can add midyear depends on whether there's a qualifying life event (QLE) or another eligibility exception (e.g., recently moved to the US, gained student status, marriage/divorce of parent, etc.).

people-ops: Docs we typically need: birth certificate or adoption paperwork (proof of relationship), current school enrollment letter or tuition invoice showing full-time status, passport + visa/I-20 for non‑US citizens, and proof of address if applicable. If you don't have an SSN yet we can proceed with SSN=TBD and you update later.

benefits-bot: Upload link: https://benefits.redwood.com/upload — select "dependent enrollment" and tag with "student". Allowed file types: pdf, jpg, png.

olivia: Thanks — small wrinkle: they're a stepchild (my partner is the custodial parent this school year). Born outside the US and currently here on F-1 with an I-20. No SSN right now. Is stepchild OK and will the I-20 + passport be fine?

jamal: Yes, stepchildren are eligible if they're your spouse/partner's child and meet the age/dependent criteria. I-20 + passport + school enrollment letter is fine. For relationship proof, we usually accept a copy of the parent's birth certificate showing parentage or a court custody/guardianship doc. If the biological parent is the spouse/partner on your enrollment, please include a short notarized statement if the usual docs are ambiguous.

people-ops: Timing notes: once you upload the docs we'll submit to the carrier. If this counts as a QLE (e.g., recently moved to US or change in custody), coverage can be effective retroactive to the QLE date; otherwise it may wait until next open enrollment. Send the date they moved/gained student status in the thread or DM.

olivia: Do dental + vision need separate paperwork? And when would payroll deductions kick in?

people-ops: Same set of docs covers medical, dental, and vision. Payroll will pick up changes the first full pay cycle after enrollment is processed — usually 1–2 pay periods. We'll tag payroll once the carrier confirms enrollment.

hr-intake: File naming convention for uploads (helps routing):
```
lastname_firstname_doc_YYYYMM.pdf
example: smith_jordan_i20_202603.pdf
```

olivia: Uploading now. I'll include an enrollment letter from the university and the I-20. Thanks for the quick help! :pray:

benefits-bot: Upload received: smith_jordan_i20_202603.pdf. Intake queue updated. Estimated intake review: 1–3 business days. We'll ping this thread once the carrier responds. :white_check_mark:
